pr_title: extmod/vfs: Add finaliser to ilistdir to close file handle.
pr_body:
When iterating over filesystem / folders with `os.iterdir()`, an open file (directory) handle is used internally. Currently this file handle is only closed once the iterator is completely drained (eg. all entries have been looped over / converted into list etc).

If a program opens an iterdir but does not loop over it, or starts to loop over the iterator but breaks out of the loop (eg `while os.iterdir(): break` or `if any(os.iterdir()`) then the handle never gets closed. 

In this state, when the iter object is cleaned up by the garbage collector this open handle can cause corruption of the filesystem. See https://github.com/micropython/micropython/issues/6568#issuecomment-819333115

Closes https://github.com/micropython/micropython/issues/6568 & https://github.com/micropython/micropython/issues/8506

I've tried to cover the reproduction description of #8506 in the unit test included here and it does appear to pass correctly with this fix in place.

I did find the root cause of this and thought I posted the outcome here, but it looks like the comment did not get posted.

The problem is that `ilistdir()` is being used without exhausting the iterator, and so the open directory descriptor never gets closed, even though the GC reclaims and reuses the memory.  The fix would be to make the `ilistdir()` iterator have a finaliser.

In the meantime, a workaround is to always exhaust the iterator, eg with `list(ilistdir())`.

Minimal code to reproduce the issue (on any port):
```python
import gc

try:
    import uos

    uos.VfsLfs2
except (ImportError, AttributeError):
    print("SKIP")
    raise SystemExit


class RAMBlockDevice:
    ERASE_BLOCK_SIZE = 1024

    def __init__(self, blocks):
        self.data = bytearray(blocks * self.ERASE_BLOCK_SIZE)

    def readblocks(self, block, buf, off):
        addr = block * self.ERASE_BLOCK_SIZE + off
        for i in range(len(buf)):
            buf[i] = self.data[addr + i]

    def writeblocks(self, block, buf, off):
        addr = block * self.ERASE_BLOCK_SIZE + off
        for i in range(len(buf)):
            self.data[addr + i] = buf[i]

    def ioctl(self, op, arg):
        if op == 4:  # block count
            return len(self.data) // self.ERASE_BLOCK_SIZE
        if op == 5:  # block size
            return self.ERASE_BLOCK_SIZE
        if op == 6:  # erase block
            return 0


def test(bdev, vfs_class):
    vfs_class.mkfs(bdev)
    vfs = vfs_class(bdev)

    for i in range(10):
        print(i)
        l = vfs.ilistdir("/")
        #list(l)  # uncomment and the bug is no longer there because the iterator is exhausted
        gc.collect()
        vfs.open("/test", "w").close()


bdev = RAMBlockDevice(30)
test(bdev, uos.VfsLfs2)
```

If `dir_open` fails then `vfs` is still non-NULL and the finaliser will run and call `dir_close`, which may do something bad.
